summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with advanced multiple sclerosis, neurogenic bladder with a suprapubic catheter, and a history of recurrent UTIs, was admitted after a witnessed seizure with tongue biting and aspiration. He was found to have hyponatremia likely due to excessive water intake, and imaging revealed encephalomalacia as a possible seizure focus. He developed aspiration pneumonia requiring antibiotics and was intubated briefly for airway protection. His sodium corrected, seizures were controlled with levetiracetam, and he improved clinically. A video swallow study showed mild aspiration initially but cleared him for ground foods and thin liquids with a recommendation to start meals with pureed foods. He was discharged home with services, on Keppra for seizure prevention, with follow-up planned for neurology, dermatology, and primary care, and instructions for wound care and baclofen pump refill.
